key_insight: Error-Conditioned Neural Solvers (ENS) improve PDE solution accuracy by feeding the model its own residual field as an input, so it learns how to correct errors instead of trying to minimize the residual with classical optimization.
engineering_relevance: ENS offers a faster, more stable alternative to hybrid physics-guided solvers for scientific computing, especially in ill-conditioned and out-of-distribution settings.
method: Input the PDE residual field directly at each iteration
Learn an iterative correction policy rather than running gradient descent or Gauss-Newton on the residual
Use the residual’s spatial structure to guide self-correction and reconstruction
evidence_signal: Across four PDE families, ENS achieved the best accuracy in most settings, with up to 10× gains on turbulent Kolmogorov flow and strong generalization under parameter shifts and cross-equation transfer.
watch_item: Performance may depend on how well the residual representation is constructed and on the training coverage of PDE families, so robustness should be checked before deployment.
